entries.appliesTo: operators making available or controlling access to AI companion chatbots for users in Washington

dutySources.disclosure-ui: Sec. 3(1) — 'An operator must provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure that an AI companion chatbot is artificially generated and not human.'
dutySources.content-safeguards: Sec. 4(1)(b) — 'Implement reasonable measures to prevent its AI companion chatbot from generating or producing sexually explicit content or suggestive dialogue with minors'; Sec. 3(3) — 'implement reasonable measures to prohibit and prevent AI companion chatbots from claiming to be human'
dutySources.crisis-protocol: Sec. 5(1) — 'An operator may not make available or deploy an AI companion chatbot unless it maintains and implements a protocol for detecting and addressing suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm by users.'

exposure.enforcer: consumer-protection-act (chapter 19.86 RCW) — unfair or deceptive act

sources.appliesTo: Sec. 2(4) — '"Operator" means any person, partnership, corporation, or entity that makes available or controls access to an AI companion chatbot for users in this state.'
sources.scope: Sec. 2(1)(a) — '"AI companion chatbot" or "AI companion" means an artificial intelligence system with a natural language interface that provides adaptive, human-like responses to user inputs, including by exhibiting anthropomorphic features, and is able to sustain a relationship across multiple interactions.'
sources.ageFocus: Sec. 3(1) — 'An operator must provide a clear and conspicuous disclosure' (duty runs to every user; Sec. 4 adds minor-specific duties)
sources.aiDisclosure: Sec. 3(2)(a)-(b) — 'At the beginning of the interaction; and' 'At least every three hours during continued interaction.'
sources.crisisProtocol: Sec. 5(2)(b) — 'Provide automated or human-mediated responses that refer users to appropriate crisis resources, including a suicide hotline or crisis text line'
sources.engagementLimits: Sec. 4(1)(c) — 'Implement reasonable measures to prohibit the use of manipulative engagement techniques, which cause the AI companion chatbot to engage in or prolong an emotional relationship with the user'
sources.contentSafeguards: Sec. 4(1)(b) — 'prevent its AI companion chatbot from generating or producing sexually explicit content or suggestive dialogue with minors'
sources.ageThreshold: Sec. 2(3) — '"Minor" means any person under 18 years of age.'
sources.enforcer: Sec. 6 — 'A violation of this chapter is not reasonable in relation to the development and preservation of business and is an unfair or deceptive act in trade or commerce and an unfair method of competition for the purpose of applying the consumer protection act, chapter 19.86 RCW'

flags: aiDisclosure coded 'periodic' (lossy multi-value): notice required both at session start and at least every three hours (Sec. 3(2)); interval tightens to at least every hour during continuous interaction for known-minor users or minor-directed chatbots (Sec. 4(2)(b))

engagementLimits and contentSafeguards duties apply only when the operator knows the user is a minor or the chatbot is directed to minors (Sec. 4(1)); disclosure and crisis-protocol duties apply to all users

Sec. 5(3) requires public disclosure, on the operator's website and in-app, of crisis-protocol details and 'the number of crisis referral notifications issued to users in the preceding calendar year' — annual transparency-reporting requirement with no matching duty key in the v1.0 vocabulary
no penaltyMax coded: enforcement is routed entirely through the consumer protection act, chapter 19.86 RCW (rule 4 — no imports)
no age-verification duty: minor provisions trigger on actual knowledge or minor-directedness, not on required age assurance
